title: Coordinate derivations, equation schemes and pointwise implicit Taylor data
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $B,N$ schemes [def-pc-scheme], with a polynomial coordinate homomorphism $c:k[w_1,\ldots,w_m,y_1,\ldots,y_r]\to\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Restrict it to each open and take its germs at every point. A coordinate derivation datum consists of $\mathbf Z$-derivations $D_i$ on sections of every open, killing $k$, sending $c(x_j)$ to $\delta_{ij}$, commuting with each other and with restriction [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For $r$ global functions $h$, define $J=\det(D_{y_j}h_i)$ and $U=D(J)$. Define the equation ideal on $U$ as the quasi-coherent ideal generated by $h_i|_U$, and define $N_h$ to be its closed subscheme, with its actual inclusion $N_h\to U\to B$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. The coordinate morphism is $B\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)\to\operatorname{Spec}k[w,y]$; the structure morphism uses the scalar restriction of $c$.
For formal series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] put $s_\phi(W_i)=W_i$, $s_\phi(Y_j)=\phi_j(W)+Y_j$ and $g_\phi(W_i)=W_i$, $g_\phi(Y_j)=\phi_j(W)$. Shift a full $T$-family coefficientwise by formal substitution. Iterate the regular $y$-derivations in increasing variable order, repeating $D_{y_j}$ exactly $\delta_j$ times; use the existing formal partial derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] and transverse coefficient extraction [def-trf-implicit-transverse-coefficient].
When $k$ has characteristic zero, a pointwise implicit Taylor datum for $(c,h,D,j:N\to B,b\in N)$ consists of the following specified data and properties; it asserts no existence. Put $L=\kappa(b)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. There are stalk derivations extending the open-section derivations, and uniquely characterized Taylor homomorphisms $\tau:\mathcal O_{B,jb}\to L[[W,Y]]$, $\tau_N:\mathcal O_{N,b}\to L[[W]]$ using [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum]. Their residues are evaluation through $j$; they send scalars to constants and coordinates to their residues plus their corresponding formal variables. There is a zero-constant $\phi\in L[[W]]^r$, equal to the centered $\tau_N$-expansion of $y|_N$, uniquely solving $h_\tau(W,\phi)=0$. There is an invertible matrix $M$ with $h_\tau=M(Y-\phi)$. There is an $L$-algebra equivalence given by substitution $Y=\phi(W)+Z$, with inverse substitution by $-\phi$, both continuous in the discrete-coefficient product topology. The kernel of the stalk restriction along $j$ is generated by $h$, and its extension by $\tau$ followed by this equivalence is $(Z)$. Substitution along the graph agrees with $\tau_N$ after stalk restriction. Taylor expansion commutes with every coordinate derivation. For every full formal $T$-family of stalk functions, its shifted $Z^\delta T^\gamma$ coefficient is $\tau_N((D_y^\delta f_\gamma)|_N)/\delta!$. The map $\tau$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and reflects equality of extended finitely generated ideals. For every field extension $L\to K$ in any specified universe, both Taylor maps remain uniquely characterized by these scalar, residue and coordinate formulas; mapping the matrix entries retains invertibility and factorization, mapping $\phi$ retains its zero-constant solution and uniqueness, and substitution and the derivative coefficient formulas commute with the coefficient map. Empty coordinate lists and nonclosed points are included.
